choices.why: Off-white three-seater on slim birch legs: the light, airy Nordic base the long wall needs.
Bentwood birch reading chair with an off-white cushion and headrest; it repeats the sofa's light wood and cream fabric.
Pale ash square table with slender splayed legs; warm and light, and it does not crowd the seating area.
Large 212x300 natural-fibre rug that holds the whole seating group and adds warm, natural texture.
Oval table, 185 cm long, on light birch crossed legs; it seats six comfortably and stays light in front of the window.
Bent birch plywood chairs, light and warm, matching the table's legs.
Woven bamboo pendant that gives warm, filtered light over the table and fits the natural palette.
Tall rice-paper column lamp with a soft, serene glow for the reading corner.
Low walnut-veneer sideboard on wooden legs; it adds warmth and long, quiet storage beside the dining area.
Sand-coloured linen curtains, light and airy, that soften the window's black frame.
Linen-look cushions in leaf green, the touch of green asked for against the cream fabrics.
Beige cable-knit throw that adds Nordic texture and warmth to the sofa.
Tall areca palm that brings lush green to the corner between the two areas.
Graphic Scandinavian botanical print with lots of white space; it lifts the white wall without overloading it.
Matte stoneware vases in off-white and soft blue-green, organic and calm in a Nordic way.

answer.why: Birch, ash and natural fibres pick up the warmth of the oak floor, while cream fabrics and touches of green give a calm, welcoming Nordic look along the whole length of the room.
